data.current_description:
Creates a remote-mode session and commits round 0, then returns a `202` ack in under 500ms. Model execution runs in the background — poll `progress_url` until the round is terminal, then read the artifacts from `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

Omit `models` and the platform curates a panel of up to your plan's seat cap (frontier / mid / cheap, one per provider family, from the active registry models your plan can run). Pass 2–3 explicit model IDs to choose the panel yourself; call `GET /api/models` to enumerate valid IDs and see which your plan includes.

Two fields are explicitly REJECTED rather than ignored: `moderator_model` (autonomous AI moderation was retired in 2026-05) and `recap_session` (round 0 alone cannot produce a session synthesis). Sending either returns `400 invalid_request`. Unrecognized keys are ignored.
data.summary_suggestion: Create a new deliberation session with initial round
data.description_suggestion:
Creates a new session and commits round 0 (initial round), returning a `202 Accepted` acknowledgment within 500ms. Model execution proceeds asynchronously in the background.

**Model Panel Selection:**
- Omit `models` to auto-curate a panel up to your plan's seat cap (one model per provider family from active registry).
- Pass 2–3 explicit model IDs to select your own panel; call `GET /api/models` to enumerate valid IDs and check plan eligibility.

**Rejected Fields:** `moderator_model` and `recap_session` are explicitly rejected (not ignored) and return `400 invalid_request`. Autonomous moderation was retired in 2026-05; round 0 alone cannot produce session synthesis.

**Async Workflow:** Returns an `Ack` with `progress_url`. Poll `GET /api/sessions/{id}/progress` until the round reaches a terminal state, then fetch full artifacts via `GET /api/sessions/{id}`.

data.current_description:
Adds a round to an existing session and returns a `202` ack; model execution runs in the background. The round reuses the session's participant panel — you cannot change models mid-session.

`snippets` is optional but is the highest-signal thing a moderator does: verbatim quotes from a prior round's responses, each tagged KEEP (preserve this), EXPLORE (dig deeper), CHALLENGE (push back), CORE (build on it), or SHIFT (this reframes the question). `quoted_model` is the model ID that originated the quote.

An `Idempotency-Key` is strongly recommended here — round-append duplication corrupts deliberation history.

`improvement_consent` and `dataset_consent` are session-level and are REJECTED on this endpoint (`400 invalid_request`) rather than silently changing consent mid-session.
data.summary_suggestion: Append a round with optional moderator snippets
data.description_suggestion:
Adds a new round to an existing session and returns a `202 Accepted` acknowledgment; model execution proceeds asynchronously in the background. The round reuses the session's existing participant panel — models cannot be changed mid-session.

**Snippets (Optional but High-Signal):** Verbatim quotes from prior round responses, each tagged with a directive:
- `KEEP`: Preserve this claim
- `EXPLORE`: Dig deeper into this
- `CHALLENGE`: Push back on this
- `CORE`: Build on this foundation
- `SHIFT`: This reframes the question

Each snippet requires `quoted_model` (the originating model ID).

**Idempotency:** Include an `Idempotency-Key` header (strongly recommended) to prevent round-append duplication, which corrupts deliberation history.

**Rejected Fields:** `improvement_consent` and `dataset_consent` are session-level and are explicitly rejected (`400 invalid_request`) rather than silently changing consent mid-session.

**When to Use:** Only use this endpoint if you need internal field names or raw round data. For standard use cases, prefer `GET /api/sessions/{id}`, which returns serialized, contract-stable round entries in `rounds[]`.

data.current_description:
Publishes the session at a public reader-deck URL that anyone with the link can view. No request body.

Idempotent — re-calling returns the same slug and URLs. The public page is a point-in-time snapshot; a share call made after new rounds were appended refreshes it at the same URL. A share never demotes an already-elevated artifact.

The first share of a long session generates any missing round takeaways before freezing the snapshot (~15–30s worst case), so a `500 share_failed` whose message says summaries are still generating is transient — retry after a moment.

`markdown_url` is the full-transcript machine-readable twin (per-round claim maps included — the review/audit surface); `brief_url` is the synthesis-only triage tier (~1–2k tokens, predictable cost).
data.description_suggestion:
Publishes the session at a public reader-deck URL accessible to anyone with the link. No request body required.

**Idempotency & Updates:** Idempotent — re-calling returns the same slug and URLs. The public page is a point-in-time snapshot; calling after new rounds are appended refreshes the snapshot at the same URL. Shares never demote already-elevated artifacts.

**Initial Share Latency:** The first share of a long session generates any missing round takeaways before freezing the snapshot (worst case ~15–30s). A `500 share_failed` response with message indicating summaries are still generating is transient — retry after a moment.

**Response URLs:**
- `markdown_url`: Full-transcript machine-readable format including per-round claim maps (review/audit surface)
